name: CPCRN Pregabalin
aliases: Chronic Prostatitis Collaborative Research Network-2 pregabalin trial
question: Does pregabalin increase six-week NIH-CPSI responder rates compared with placebo in men with chronic prostatitis/chronic pelvic pain syndrome?

design.population: 324 men aged at least 18 years with pelvic pain during at least 3 of the preceding 6 months, NIH-CPSI score at least 15 at screening and randomization, and calculated creatinine clearance at least 60 mL/min/1.73 m² were enrolled at 10 North American tertiary centers.
design.locator: Full text, Methods, Participants and Study Design; Table 1

verdictNote: The prespecified six-point NIH-CPSI responder comparison missed significance (P=.07).
takeaway: In men with chronic prostatitis/chronic pelvic pain syndrome, six weeks of pregabalin versus placebo did not significantly increase the prespecified six-point NIH-CPSI responder rate (47.2% versus 35.8%; P=.07); several secondary symptom measures favored pregabalin.

delivery.label: Dose escalation
delivery.value: Pregabalin 150 mg/day (50 mg orally three times daily) for two weeks, then 300 mg/day (100 mg three times daily) for two weeks, then 600 mg/day (200 mg three times daily) for two weeks; a participant could remain at a tolerated dose.

delivery.label: Completion and highest-dose exposure
delivery.value: 313/324 (96.6%) completed six-week follow-up; 154/218 (70.6%) in the pregabalin arm and 82/106 (77.4%) in the placebo arm took the highest dose for at least one week.
